Title: Name: SFCM for Anki
Description: Decided: the project is called 'SFCM for Anki'. The 'for Anki' suffix makes clear it is an unofficial companion (Anki is a trademark of Ankitects). Add a README disclaimer saying the project is not affiliated with Anki or Ankitects.
Acceptance Criteria: GitHub org/repo and domain reserved; README disclaimer present

Title: License: AGPL-3.0
Description: Decided: AGPL-3.0-or-later, matching the official anki Python package the engine links. Every dependency must be AGPL-compatible (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0, LGPL, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0). GPL-2.0-only code is not allowed. Add SPDX headers to source files.
Acceptance Criteria: LICENSE committed; SPDX headers; cargo-deny, pip-licenses and license-checker run in CI and fail on incompatible licenses

Title: Architecture: Tauri 2 + Rust shell + Python engine
Description: Decided (ADR-001). The Rust (Tauri 2) shell owns windows, file dialogs, the OS keychain, the updater and engine supervision. The React/TypeScript webview owns all UI. The Python engine owns Anki I/O (official anki package), LLM calls, document parsing, jobs and the app database. The shell never parses documents and the engine never touches the UI.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR-001 merged in docs/adr

Title: Monorepo scaffolding
Description: Layout: /app (Tauri 2, Cargo workspace), /ui (React 18 + Vite + TypeScript strict, pnpm), /engine (Python 3.12, uv, src layout), /docs, /prompts, /evals. Tooling: rustfmt and clippy (-D warnings); Biome for TS lint and format; ruff (lint and format) and pyright strict for Python. A justfile is the single task runner (just dev, just test, just lint, just build). Pre-commit hooks run through lefthook.
Acceptance Criteria: Fresh clone: 'just setup && just dev' opens the app with a live engine on Windows, macOS and Linux; 'just lint' is clean

Title: CI build and test matrix
Description: GitHub Actions matrix: ubuntu-22.04 (oldest glibc baseline for Linux packages), windows-latest, a macOS arm64 runner and a macOS Intel runner. Cache with Swatinem/rust-cache, astral-sh/setup-uv and pnpm store. Jobs: lint, cargo test, pytest, vitest, a license check (see A02), and a full 'tauri build' on main and release branches. Use Conventional Commits with release-please to produce changelogs and version bumps.
Acceptance Criteria: Required checks green on all 4 OS targets; PR-to-green under 15 min with warm cache

Title: Bundle and supervise the Python engine
Description: Freeze the engine with PyInstaller in --onedir mode (onefile re-extracts on every launch, starts slowly and triggers antivirus false positives) and ship it as a Tauri resource. Rust spawns it with std::process, waits for a 'ready' handshake carrying the engine and protocol versions, restarts it with backoff on crash, and kills its process tree when the app exits (Job Object on Windows, process group on Unix). Sign every bundled binary inside the macOS app before notarization.
Acceptance Criteria: Installed app starts the engine in under 2 s on all OSes without a system Python; killing the engine mid-job shows a notice and auto-restarts; no orphan processes after quit; engine bundle under 120 MB

Title: UI-to-engine IPC protocol
Description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, newline-delimited, in the style of LSP: requests, $/progress notifications, $/cancelRequest. The Rust shell is a thin router between Tauri commands and events and the engine pipe; it never interprets payloads. Schemas are defined once in pydantic v2, exported as JSON Schema and generated into TypeScript types with json-schema-to-typescript. Protocol version is checked at handshake.
Acceptance Criteria: Generated TS types committed and CI fails on drift; cancel stops an in-flight LLM call within 1 s; protocol mismatch shows an upgrade message

Title: Secrets, settings and app database
Description: API keys live only in the OS keychain through the Rust keyring crate (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service on Linux). The engine requests a key over IPC when it needs one and keeps it in memory only. Settings, sessions, job queue and the ingest manifest live in one SQLite database in the Tauri app-data directory, owned by the engine, with numbered migrations. Logs pass through a redaction filter.
Acceptance Criteria: Grep of logs, database and crash output after a full run finds no key material; migrations tested from every previous schema

Title: LLM provider layer
Description: Thin in-house interface in the engine (no LiteLLM). Adapters: Anthropic (official SDK; default generation model claude-opus-5-5 (user can switch to claude-sonnet-5-5 in settings), claude-haiku-5-5 as the eval judge), OpenAI (official SDK), and OpenAI-compatible endpoints covering Ollama and LM Studio for fully local use. Cards come back as structured output validated by pydantic, with one repair retry. Use Anthropic prompt caching for the shared rubric prompt with the Message Batches API for large folder and deck jobs deferred to the job runner (D12). Count tokens and cost per request. A per-project 'local only' switch blocks every cloud adapter.
Acceptance Criteria: Same generation request passes on Anthropic, OpenAI and Ollama; 'local only' enforced by a test that fails on any non-localhost request; batch jobs survive app restart

Title: Prompt library and card-quality rubric
Description: Prompts are Jinja2 templates in /prompts with semantic versions and a changelog. A shared rubric based on the 20 rules of formulating knowledge (one fact per card, no ambiguity, no yes/no, short answers, cloze discipline, context cues) feeds all three features. Card output uses one JSON schema covering every note type (Basic, reversed, type-in, Cloze, Image Occlusion) plus the Why, Example, Mnemonic and Source fields. Each card records the prompt version that produced it.
Acceptance Criteria: Prompts load by name and version; schema published in docs; rubric doc reviewed by at least one heavy Anki user

Title: Card quality evaluation harness
Description: pytest-based evals in /evals. Golden sources are openly licensed material (OpenStax textbooks, CC BY; selected Wikipedia articles, CC BY-SA) plus 3 public shared decks for improver tests. Metrics: schema validity, rule-lint pass rate, duplicate rate, faithfulness to source and atomicity (LLM judge with a fixed model), cost per accepted card. Runs nightly with a repository secret, and on PRs that touch /prompts or /engine/llm.
Acceptance Criteria: 'just eval' prints a scored report; CI posts the score delta on prompt PRs; any regression over 5% is flagged

Title: Contributor experience
Description: CONTRIBUTING with dev setup per OS, Contributor Covenant 2.1, SECURITY.md with a private reporting address, GitHub issue forms (bug, feature, card-quality report with sample input), PR template, and a label scheme mirroring the roadmap epics. Use a DCO sign-off instead of a CLA, which suits an AGPL project. Mark good-first-issue tasks.
Acceptance Criteria: A new contributor can run the app locally within 15 minutes following the docs (tested by one outside volunteer)

Title: Privacy policy and network allowlist
Description: No telemetry by default. Outbound traffic is limited to: the chosen LLM provider, the update server (GitHub Releases) and localhost:8765 (AnkiConnect). Lock down the Tauri content security policy and capabilities (no arbitrary shell, filesystem access scoped to user-chosen folders). PRIVACY.md lists exactly what text leaves the machine and when.
Acceptance Criteria: PRIVACY.md published; a network test run records only allowlisted hosts; Tauri capability files reviewed

Title: UI internationalization
Description: i18next with ICU message format in the UI, with English and Spanish as the first two locales. The engine returns error codes and parameters, never display strings. The card language is a separate setting from the UI language. Weblate (free hosting for open-source projects) handles community translations.
Acceptance Criteria: All UI strings externalized; Spanish complete; a pseudo-locale test catches hard-coded strings

Title: Pin and track the anki package version
Description: Pin the official anki PyPI package to one Anki release and record the oldest Anki desktop, AnkiDroid and AnkiMobile versions that import our packages. A scheduled CI job tests the next Anki release when it ships and opens an issue if a round-trip breaks. Document the policy for bumping the pin.
Acceptance Criteria: Compatibility table in docs; scheduled job builds, exports and re-imports a sample deck against the latest anki release

Title: Note type registry
Description: Bundle note types with stable model IDs: Basic, Basic (and reversed), Basic (optional reversed), Basic (type in the answer), Cloze, and Image Occlusion. Each has app-styled templates and fields for Why, Example, Mnemonic and Source.
Acceptance Criteria: Each type imports into Anki desktop and renders front and back correctly

Title: Write .apkg packages
Description: Build packages with the official anki package: create a temporary collection, add the bundled note types and notes, then export through Anki's own exporter. That gives the modern format, media, tags, nested decks (::), Image Occlusion and stable GUIDs derived from content IDs, so re-imports update notes instead of duplicating them. Offer a legacy-compatible export option for older mobile clients.
Acceptance Criteria: Package imports cleanly in Anki desktop 24.x/25.x, AnkiDroid and AnkiMobile; re-import updates and does not duplicate

Title: Read .apkg and .colpkg packages
Description: Use the official anki package to open packages in a temporary collection and read notes, models, media and review state (read-only).
Acceptance Criteria: Reads a 20k-note shared deck in under 30 s

Title: AnkiConnect client
Description: Detect a running Anki and check the AnkiConnect version. Wrap findNotes, notesInfo, addNotes, updateNoteFields, changeDeck, storeMediaFile and sync. Degrade gracefully when Anki is closed.
Acceptance Criteria: Integration tests against a real Anki in CI (Linux, headless)

Title: Card themes as note-type CSS
Description: Build themes into note-type templates and CSS instead of inline styles, with night-mode support (.nightMode), mobile breakpoints and print-safe fonts. Ship 3 starter themes.
Acceptance Criteria: All themes pass visual checks on desktop, AnkiDroid and AnkiMobile in light and night mode

Title: Media pipeline
Description: Import images and audio, resize and compress, dedupe by hash, and name files the way Anki expects. Clean up orphaned media.
Acceptance Criteria: Media appears on cards after import on all clients

Title: Math and code rendering
Description: Emit MathJax delimiters for math. Pre-render syntax highlighting with Pygments to static HTML and CSS, because highlighting scripts are unreliable on mobile clients.
Acceptance Criteria: Math and code samples render identically on all clients

Title: Sanitize generated card HTML
Description: Anki executes JavaScript in card templates and fields, so all LLM output must pass an allowlist sanitizer (bleach on the engine, DOMPurify in the UI). Treat source documents as data to guard against prompt injection.
Acceptance Criteria: Fuzz tests show no script or event handler can reach a field

Title: Text-to-speech and audio options
Description: Add an optional {{tts}} template variant for language decks, and optionally pre-generated audio files via a provider.
Acceptance Criteria: TTS cards speak on desktop and AnkiDroid

Title: Client compatibility QA checklist
Description: Write a manual and automated checklist covering Anki desktop (Win, macOS, Linux), AnkiDroid, AnkiMobile and AnkiWeb review.
Acceptance Criteria: Checklist runs before every release

Title: Port Card Studio UI to React
Description: Rebuild the existing Anki Card Studio prototype (source form, settings, deck grid, flip preview) as React components backed by the engine.
Acceptance Criteria: Feature parity with the prototype

Title: Anki template renderer for preview
Description: TypeScript renderer for Anki template syntax: {{Field}}, {{FrontSide}}, {{cloze:}}, {{hint:}}, {{type:}}, {{#cond}}. Previews use the real note-type templates and CSS.
Acceptance Criteria: Snapshot tests match Anki's output for each bundled note type

Title: Note type picker in the form
Description: Expose every bundled note type with an explanation of when to use each one. Claude may also choose the type per fact in auto mode.
Acceptance Criteria: User can generate any bundled type; auto mode picks a sensible mix

Title: Generate from topic or pasted text
Description: Options: card count, type mix, depth, language, extras (why, example, mnemonic), tags. Stream progress and allow stopping.
Acceptance Criteria: Generates N valid notes; Stop cancels the provider request

Title: Rich field editor
Description: Edit fields with bold, italic, code, math, images and cloze insertion (Ctrl+Shift+C as in Anki). The preview updates live.
Acceptance Criteria: All formatting round-trips through export unchanged

Title: Per-card AI actions
Description: Actions on each card: regenerate, split into atomic cards, simplify, add example, convert to cloze, translate.
Acceptance Criteria: Each action produces a reviewable diff before replacing the card

Title: Image occlusion creator
Description: Upload an image and draw rectangle, ellipse or polygon masks to create Image Occlusion notes (Anki 23.10+ format), with an AI-suggested masks option for labelled diagrams.
Acceptance Criteria: IO notes review correctly in Anki desktop and AnkiDroid

Title: Deck, sub-deck and tag manager
Description: Pick or create a deck path and use a hierarchical tag picker. Optionally embed an FSRS deck-options preset in the package.
Acceptance Criteria: Exported notes land in the chosen deck with the chosen tags

Title: Export targets
Description: Export to an .apkg file, send directly to a running Anki via AnkiConnect, or copy as TSV (fallback).
Acceptance Criteria: All three paths tested end to end

Title: Local sessions and autosave
Description: Keep drafts in the app database and show a recent-sessions list. Nothing is lost on crash.
Acceptance Criteria: Kill the app mid-edit; work restored on relaunch

Title: Folder sources with watch mode
Description: Add one or more folders with include and exclude globs. Watch mode (watchdog) queues changed files automatically.
Acceptance Criteria: Adding a file to a watched folder queues it within 5 s

Title: Parse Markdown and plain text
Description: Handle front matter, headings, lists, code blocks, Obsidian wikilinks and embeds.
Acceptance Criteria: Golden-file tests on a sample Obsidian vault

Title: Parse DOCX, ODT, PPTX and EPUB
Description: Use pandoc or python-docx and python-pptx. Keep the heading structure and extract embedded images.
Acceptance Criteria: Structure preserved in golden tests

Title: Parse PDF
Description: Use PyMuPDF (AGPL-compatible) for text with layout, page numbers, figures and tables. Detect multi-column layouts.
Acceptance Criteria: Lecture-slide and textbook PDFs produce clean ordered text

Title: OCR for scanned documents
Description: Optional Tesseract OCR for scanned PDFs and images, with language packs.
Acceptance Criteria: Scanned PDF yields usable text; feature off by default

Title: Structure-aware chunking
Description: Split documents by heading and section into token-budgeted chunks. Each chunk keeps a source anchor (file, heading, page) that fills the card's Source field.
Acceptance Criteria: Every generated card links back to its source location

Title: Incremental processing manifest
Description: Hash files and chunks so only changed chunks are reprocessed. When a source is deleted or edited, flag the cards it produced.
Acceptance Criteria: Second run on an unchanged folder makes zero LLM calls

Title: Semantic deduplication
Description: Use local embeddings (e.g. fastembed) to find near-duplicates within a batch and against the target deck, with a configurable threshold.
Acceptance Criteria: Re-ingesting overlapping notes adds no duplicate cards in tests

Title: Map folders to decks
Description: Folder tree becomes the sub-deck tree. Front matter (deck, tags, note type, skip) overrides per file.
Acceptance Criteria: Mapping preview shown before the run

Title: Review queue
Description: Approve, edit or reject generated cards, grouped by source file, with bulk actions and keyboard shortcuts.
Acceptance Criteria: 1000 pending cards stay responsive

Title: Cost estimate and budget cap
Description: Estimate tokens and cost before a run and stop at a user-set budget.
Acceptance Criteria: Estimate within 20% of actual on the eval set

Title: Job runner
Description: Persistent queue with pause, resume and cancel. Survives crashes and enforces rate limits per provider.
Acceptance Criteria: Kill during a run; resume completes without duplicates

Title: Use source figures on cards
Description: Extract diagrams from PDF and DOCX as card media, and optionally create image-occlusion notes from labelled figures.
Acceptance Criteria: Figures appear on the relevant cards

Title: Headless CLI
Description: Command such as 'app ingest ./notes --deck Bio --out bio.apkg' that reuses the engine, for cron or scheduled runs without the UI.
Acceptance Criteria: CLI documented; runs on all 3 OSes in CI

Title: Import decks to improve
Description: Three inputs: shared-deck .apkg downloaded from AnkiWeb, a full .colpkg collection export, or the live collection via AnkiConnect. Do not log into or scrape AnkiWeb (terms of service); the user downloads the files or syncs through Anki.
Acceptance Criteria: Each input loads into the analyzer

Title: Deck quality analyzer
Description: Rule checks plus LLM review per note: multiple facts, ambiguity, overlong answers, yes/no questions, missing context, typos, duplicates, broken media, formatting junk. Adds a leech-aware priority using review stats.
Acceptance Criteria: Report with a score per note and per deck, filterable by issue

Title: Coverage gap analysis
Description: Cluster the deck by topic and propose missing concepts. Optionally compare against a reference document or syllabus.
Acceptance Criteria: Gap list with proposed new cards ready for the review queue

Title: Improvement proposals
Description: Generate field-level changes as diffs: rewrite, split, merge, add why, example or mnemonic, convert to cloze, fix formatting.
Acceptance Criteria: Every proposal is a diff; nothing is applied automatically

Title: Diff review UI
Description: Side-by-side rendered before and after view. Accept or reject per change, bulk accept by issue type, and undo.
Acceptance Criteria: Reviewer can process 100 proposals in under 10 minutes

Title: Scheduling-safe write-back
Description: Edit notes in place so review history survives: updateNoteFields over AnkiConnect, or re-import an .apkg with the same GUIDs and newer modification times. Splits add new notes and can suspend the original.
Acceptance Criteria: Automated test proves review logs and intervals unchanged after edits

Title: Restyle onto app themes
Description: Migrate notes to the app note types with a field mapping (Anki's change-note-type), which keeps scheduling for mapped cards.
Acceptance Criteria: Restyled deck keeps all review history

Title: Automatic backup and rollback
Description: Take a .colpkg or .apkg snapshot before any write-back, with one-click restore.
Acceptance Criteria: Rollback restores byte-identical notes

Title: Shared-deck attribution and licensing
Description: Show the shared deck's author and license, keep attribution in a field, and warn before re-sharing an improved deck.
Acceptance Criteria: Attribution preserved through export

Title: Media audit
Description: Find missing, unused and oversized media, and offer compression.
Acceptance Criteria: Audit report with fix actions

Title: Large-deck performance
Description: Batch and resume processing for decks over 10k notes, with a cost estimate and a sampling mode (analyze a 5% sample first).
Acceptance Criteria: 20k-note deck analyzed without UI freeze; resumable

Title: macOS signing and notarization
Description: Requires an Apple Developer ID ($99/yr). Produce universal or per-architecture DMG builds, notarized in CI.
Acceptance Criteria: Gatekeeper opens the app without warnings

Title: Windows installer and signing
Description: Build MSI or NSIS installers with Tauri and sign them (Azure Trusted Signing or an OV certificate) to avoid SmartScreen warnings.
Acceptance Criteria: Signed installer installs and uninstalls cleanly

Title: Linux packages
Description: Ship AppImage, .deb and .rpm, then a Flathub submission.
Acceptance Criteria: Installs on Ubuntu LTS and Fedora; Flathub PR opened

Title: Auto-update
Description: Tauri updater with signed update manifests on GitHub Releases, plus stable and beta channels.
Acceptance Criteria: App updates itself from beta to the next beta

Title: User documentation site
Description: Cover install, provider and API-key setup, AnkiConnect setup, each of the three workflows, FAQ and troubleshooting.
Acceptance Criteria: Docs site deployed from repo

Title: Accessibility pass
Description: Full keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, contrast in both themes and reduced motion.
Acceptance Criteria: axe checks pass; manual screen-reader walkthrough done

Title: Opt-in error reports
Description: Opt-in crash and error reporting with scrubbing, so no card content or file paths are sent.
Acceptance Criteria: Off by default; scrubbing tested

Title: Public beta and 1.0 launch
Description: Run the beta with study communities (r/Anki, med-school and language groups), collect feedback, triage, then release 1.0.
Acceptance Criteria: 1.0 tagged; release notes published
